name: Game Booster
author: Drandox
description: Cleans memory, frees old map graphics, and boosts FPS with FPS Booster and lighter scenery.
longDescription:
Boosts your FPS and stops memory build-up over long gaming sessions. No more restarts because hidden leftovers keep eating up your free RAM.

## What it does

- **Memory cleanup:** similar to Floor Sweep, done differently: in dungeons it cleans on the victory screen or the exit countdown (while the game waits), in town once loading has finished, and only when enough has piled up, so it never gets in the way of loading or fights. It works on its own, and it gets along well with Floor Sweep: if you use Floor Sweep, Game Booster happily leaves this part to it.
- **Leftover cleanup:** removes hidden leftovers and caches that keep piling up as you play, a nice extra next to Floor Sweep.
- **FPS Booster** (Settings > Mods, on by default): makes skill effects and ultimates much lighter to draw, so big fights stay smooth. Turn it off for the full glow effects.
- **Lighter scenery** (Settings > Mods, on by default): more FPS by leaving out what is only decoration. In dungeons it hides decorative scenery (grass, bushes, bricks, burn marks); it also turns off the town animations, the ultimate background fade and pickup pop animations. Rarity backgrounds stay. Damage numbers, health bars and skills stay as they are. Turn it off to see the full scenery.
- **Freeze background animations** (Settings > Mods, on by default): stops looping background animations in dungeons, such as arena crowds, torches and banners, on their current frame, so they don't have to be redrawn every frame. Mostly helps PCs with a weaker graphics card. Characters, monsters and skills keep moving.
- **Hide shadows** (Settings > Mods, on by default): hides shadows drawn as separate pieces in dungeons, mostly under props; each one costs an extra pass of pixels. The shadows of heroes and monsters are part of their own art and stay. Turn it off to see them.
- **Lighter ultimates** (Settings > Mods, on by default): ultimates play without their big full-screen effects, the heaviest animations in the game. The ultimate itself, its damage and its sound stay. Turn it off to see the full effects.
- **Free old map graphics at** (Settings > Mods, on by default at 1.2 GB): farm for hours without going back to town. The game keeps the graphics of every map you have played for the whole session; its Haxe heap is kept under the limit you choose (1.0 to 2.0 GB, or Never). The Haxe heap is the memory of the game's code, about half of what Task Manager shows for the game, so a 1.2 GB limit means about 2-2.5 GB in Task Manager. Leftover memory is cleared first; only if the heap is still above the limit are graphics freed: maps you have not played for a while first, then every map but the one you are on. This only happens right after a map loads or on the victory screen or the 5 second exit countdown (while the game waits), never during a fight, and only when at least 100 MB has piled up since the last clear, so it doesn't cause stutters or pauses that free nothing. Maps you return to simply load again, like the first time. Heroes, effects and menus are never freed, so a very low limit may not always be reachable.
- **Performance log** (Settings > Mods, off by default): one line a minute about how the game ran, handy for comparing or reporting lag. The README on GitHub explains how to read it.
